samples.summary: Clear formatting no longer strips `href`, removing the only bulk way to drop attacker-supplied hyperlinks from a document
samples.evidence: `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:300-315) drops the `href: undefined` key, and `TextEditor.clearFormatting` (text-editor.ts:3426) now shares that constant, so neither the toolbar button, the Cmd+\ shortcut nor the slides text-box clear removes a hyperlink any more. Hrefs enter the model from untrusted sources without any scheme check: pasted HTML (`packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:610-613` and `:711-716` assign `style.href = el.getAttribute('href')` verbatim), the internal clipboard payload (`clipboard.ts:148-149`), and remote collaborators (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:194`, `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:94`). Before this change, selecting a pasted region and hitting Clear formatting stripped every `javascript:`/`data:` href in one action; afterwards the only removal command is `removeLink`, which is caret-only and one link at a time (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3737-3743`, via `findLinkRunAt`), and it cannot reach the zero-length `href` residue at all (documented in `model/caret-style.ts:61-69`), so such an href becomes permanently unremovable. I could not turn this into an exploit: every consumer I traced gates on `isSafeUrl` — Ctrl+click and view-only click (`text-editor.ts:1822`, `:2176`), the link popover anchor (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:217,224`), PDF annotations (`export/pdf-painter.ts:854`), markdown (`serialize/markdown.ts:248`) and PPTX export (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:333`). So this is a defense-in-depth loss, not a live vulnerability: a future or missed consumer that renders an href without the gate is now guaranteed to see un-strippable hostile URLs.

samples.summary: Pasted/imported hrefs are stored in the model with no scheme allowlist; the change removes the mitigation that used to compensate
samples.evidence: `parseHtmlToBlocks` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:609-613) and `collectInlines` (:711-716) copy `<a href>` straight onto `Inline.style.href`, and `sanitizeInlineStyle` (:148-149) accepts any string, so `javascript:alert(1)` or `data:text/html,...` can be persisted into the CRDT by a paste from an attacker-controlled page (or by a collaborator writing the attribute directly through Yorkie). Validation is deferred entirely to each consumer's `isSafeUrl` call, which today is complete (editor click, popover, PDF/markdown/PPTX export) — but this diff removes the one bulk scrub (`href` in `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`) that let a user clean such a document, making the missing input-side gate the sole line of defence. Validating (or at least normalising) the scheme at ingestion, as `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:567` already does with its allowlist, would remove the dependency on every future consumer remembering the gate.
searchedFor: grep 'isSafeUrl' across the repo (found gates in text-editor.ts:1822/2176, pdf-painter.ts:854, markdown.ts:248, docs-link-popover.tsx:217/224, url-detect.ts)
